_readme: Adversarial declarations for scripts/context_manifest.py. Authored to make the
producer return a WRONG answer, not to mirror the shipped corpus: a suite that
only parses real artifacts proves the corpus is clean, never that the tool is
NOTE on the CRLF/LF twin fixtures: they are deliberately NOT committed here.
This repo's .gitattributes is `* text=auto` with core.autocrlf=true, so a
committed CRLF file is normalised on the way in and checked out with the
platform's endings — both twins would arrive identical and the test would pass
vacuously. Committing a real CRLF twin would need a `-text` exemption, which is
exactly the attribute that breaks rev()'s equality with `git hash-object`. The
twins are therefore materialised byte-for-byte at test time instead.

ordered_two.why: declaration order is content; the reversed twin below must differ

ordered_two_permuted.why: same set, opposite order - MUST register as a content difference

absent_is_retained.why: absence by design is normal: rev null, row retained, no exception

duplicate_paths.why: the same path declared twice is two deliveries, not one
